analyst_view.overall: League leaders Dortmund (24 points, unbeaten in the league) host fifth-placed Leverkusen (19 points) on Sunday evening in a top-of-the-table game. Niko Kovac's side are unbeaten at home since August and very tight at the back (seven goals conceded in ten games, five of their seven league wins by a single goal); Serhou Guirassy is back from a thigh strain and came off the bench in Tuesday's 1-1 at Arsenal, while Emre Can, Konstantelias, Lerma and Inacio are out, which the numbers already count. Carles Martinez Novell's Leverkusen have won their last two (4-0 v Paderborn, 2-1 v Cologne) with Patrik Schick on nine league goals, but they play a Europa League game away at Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday evening, leaving three days and a flight before Sunday; Terrier and Guela Doue are injured and Eichhorn is still building fitness. The numbers already add for Leverkusen's high recent shot and corner counts, but not for that short turnaround, so I trim goals and shots on target a little. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.9 for Dortmund. Dortmund under Kovac play tight games (seven conceded in ten, most wins by one goal), and Leverkusen arrive three days after a Europa League trip to Zagreb, which the numbers do not see; Guirassy's return gives Dortmund their main striker back, but he is only just fit. I lean a little lower, to about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 5.1 for Dortmund, and already add for Leverkusen's 45 corners in their last six. Quansah filling in at right-back for the injured Doue changes little about Leverkusen's wide play, and Dortmund's 4-5-1 is built on control rather than crossing. I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Dortmund have picked up only six cards in six games and Leverkusen 15, and the numbers already balance those trends; a top game between two possession sides is not a grudge match, and no referee has been named yet. I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 14.6 for Dortmund, already boosted 15% for Leverkusen's 110 shots in six. Leverkusen's tired legs after Zagreb could cost a few shots, but Dortmund at home with Guirassy back may shoot a little more, so these roughly cancel and I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target, 5.3 for Dortmund. Dortmund allow few clear chances (25 on target conceded in six games), and Leverkusen's sharpness after a Thursday away game in Europe is a fair doubt, while Terrier is still out. I take a little off, to about 9.2.
